subject: Art & Design
title: Hick's Law: Too Many Choices Paralyze Users
description: A quick, practical guide to Hick's Law: Too Many Choices Paralyze Users.

hook.text: A jam store offered 24 flavors — 3% bought. The next day they offered 6 flavors — 30% bought. Fewer options, more sales.

buildup.text: Hick's Law states: the more choices you present, the longer it takes to make a decision.

discovery.text: Decision time increases logarithmically with the number of options. 2× choices ≠ 2× decision time, but it grows.

twist.text: Netflix shows thousands of options but curates them into small rows of 5-10. Choice architecture hides complexity.

climax.text: Apple's product line is deliberately tiny: one phone in three sizes. Google's homepage has one search bar.

punchline.text: The best design doesn't add options. It removes the unnecessary ones.

quiz.question: What does Hick's Law predict about user behavior?
options: More choices increase decision time and can paralyze users
Users always prefer the maximum number of options
Choices have no effect on decision speed

details.summary: Hick's Law states that decision time increases logarithmically with the number of choices. Too many options overwhelm users, causing decision paralysis and abandonment. Effective design limits choices, uses progressive disclosure, and highlights recommended options to guide decisions efficiently.
details.whyItMatters: More options seem better but actually decrease satisfaction and increase anxiety. Hick's Law explains why simple interfaces with fewer choices consistently outperform feature-rich alternatives in user engagement and conversion.
takeaways: Decision time increases with the number of available choices
Too many options cause paralysis and abandonment
Limiting choices and highlighting recommendations aids decisions

faq.question: What is the famous jam study about choice overload?
faq.answer: Psychologists Sheena Iyengar and Mark Lepper found that shoppers shown 24 jam varieties were far less likely to purchase than those shown 6. The large display attracted more attention but produced fewer sales. Too many options created evaluation anxiety that prevented action.

faq.question: How does progressive disclosure reduce choice overload?
faq.answer: Progressive disclosure shows only essential options initially, revealing advanced choices when needed. A search bar shows basic results first; filters appear on request. This approach serves beginners with simplicity while giving power users full control, without overwhelming either group.
